lead: Washington plumbing deals with rain, soft water and older homes west of the Cascades, and cold, dry winters to the east. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers statewide.
risk: older pipes and root-filled sewer lines in Seattle-area homes, wet crawl spaces and frozen pipes east of the Cascades
risk_short: old pipes, sewer roots and frozen pipes
why: Western Washington's rain keeps soil wet much of the year, which is hard on crawl spaces, sump pumps and sewer lines. Older Seattle and Tacoma homes often have galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals invaded by roots.

Eastern Washington, including Spokane and the Tri-Cities, has cold winters that freeze pipes and harder water than the west side. The state sits in an earthquake zone, so water heater strapping matters. Plumbers get their certificates from the Department of Labor and Industries.
problems: Prewar homes west of the Cascades
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Check crawl-space drainage before the rainy season.
Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Disconnect hoses before the first freeze.
areas: Calls come from Seattle, Tacoma, Bellevue, Everett, Vancouver, Spokane, the Tri-Cities and rural Washington.

faq.a: The Washington State Department of Labor and Industries issues plumber certificates, and plumbing contractors must also register with L&I. You can check both online.
